name: Flesch Reading Ease
description: Scores the readability of English text from sentence length and syllables per word (Flesch 1948); higher is easier.
notes: 60–70 is plain English; below 30 is very difficult.

name: Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level
description: Converts the same counts into a US school grade (Kincaid et al. 1975); used for military manuals and insurance policies.
notes: Grade 8 is readable by most adults.

name: Gunning Fog Index

variables.label: Words of three or more syllables

description: Estimates the years of education needed to understand a text on first reading (Gunning 1952).
notes: Aim for 12 or below for a general audience.

name: SMOG Grade

variables.label: Words of three or more syllables

description: Estimates reading grade from polysyllabic words per 30 sentences (McLaughlin 1969); favoured for health information.
notes: Needs at least 30 sentences for full accuracy.

name: Coleman–Liau Index
description: Estimates reading grade from letters and sentences per 100 words, avoiding syllable counting (Coleman and Liau 1975).

name: Automated Readability Index
description: Estimates reading grade from characters per word and words per sentence (Smith and Senter 1967).
notes: Designed for real-time monitoring of typewriters.
